choices.pr_choice: Change is confined to the single existing file LinearIsometry.lean.
choices.status_reason: The goal concerns the variable block of this file.

choices.pr_choice: Remove the fourth-ring variables from the top block and re-declare them in local `section`s around the two users (rather than e.g. explicit binders on the theorems, which an earlier revision used).
choices.excerpt: Each of the two theorems now sits in a small `section` that declares only the variables that theorem needs.
choices.consequence: Explicit binders versus sections changes the theorems' signature layout, the variable-inclusion behaviour, and readability. Which mechanism is chosen also affects the measured performance.

choices.pr_choice: Trim only the fourth-ring data (R₄, E₄, their six homs and 15 instance binders). The first three rings are left in the top block.
choices.excerpt: variable {R R₂ R₃ E E₂ E₃ F 𝓕 : Type*} [Semiring R] [Semiring R₂] [Semiring R₃]
choices.visibility_reason: The brief leaves the question open (section 4).
choices.consequence: Trimming more (e.g. the third ring) could give more speed-up but would change the types of other declarations.

choices.pr_choice: Statements are textually unchanged. Only the order of implicit and instance binders shifts, because the fourth-ring variables now come after the other variables.
choices.excerpt: Only the order of their implicit and instance binders changes. Mathlib contains no `@`-application of either theorem.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief only asks that hypotheses and explicit arguments be preserved and lists binder order as an open question.
choices.consequence: Matters only to @-style uses or to downstream automation. The description says there are none in Mathlib.

choices.pr_choice: The comp_assoc section declares only the three composition-triple instances and the homs it needs (σ₁₄, σ₂₄, σ₃₄). It omits the inverse-pair instances and the reverse homs.
choices.excerpt:
{σ₁₄ : R →+* R₄} {σ₂₄ : R₂ →+* R₄} {σ₃₄ : R₃ →+* R₄}
  [RingHomCompTriple σ₁₂ σ₂₄ σ₁₄] [RingHomCompTriple σ₂₃ σ₃₄ σ₂₄] [RingHomCompTriple σ₁₃ σ₃₄ σ₁₄]
choices.consequence: The minimal hypothesis set determines how general comp_assoc is. Keeping the old full set would leave the statement unchanged but weaker than necessary, and would remove part of the speed-up.

choices.pr_choice: The trans_assoc section keeps all six inverse-pair instances and the six composition-triple instances, i.e. the full fourth-ring set, rather than trimming further.
choices.excerpt: [RingHomInvPair σ₁₄ σ₄₁] [RingHomInvPair σ₄₁ σ₁₄] [RingHomInvPair σ₂₄ σ₄₂]
choices.consequence: Needed for the equivalence structure to exist. The exact set is whatever the type of the equivalences requires.

choices.pr_choice: Each theorem gets its own section, named `assoc`, placed directly around the theorem where it already is. The variable declarations are duplicated across the two sections rather than shared.
choices.consequence: Section names and position are cosmetic. A single shared section is possible but would force the other declarations in between to see the variables or the two theorems to move.

choices.where: all other declarations in the file
choices.pr_choice: Leave every other declaration's type, proof and position untouched.
choices.excerpt: A dump of all constant types in the module shows that every other declaration keeps its exact type.
choices.status_reason: Section 3 of the brief: other declarations keep their exact type.
choices.visibility_reason: It is a preservation requirement the designer must know.
choices.consequence: Changing other types would be an API change for downstream users.

choices.pr_choice: Justification by standalone timing (9.08 s to 7.10 s) with a pending !bench rerun. No measurement threshold is part of the change.
choices.excerpt: Standalone elaboration of the file goes from 9.08 s to 7.10 s (medians of 6 interleaved runs, −22 %).
choices.visibility_reason: Numbers are omitted from the brief; only the aim of faster elaboration is stated.

feasibility_reason: The goal (make the file cheaper to elaborate by not carrying fourth-ring data in unrelated declarations, with all types preserved) can be stated without naming the section mechanism, the section names, the minimal hypothesis sets or the binder-order consequence. The brief has to name the two theorems that use the fourth ring. They exist at base and are the places the change concerns. Naming them hints at the scoping route but does not fix it.
brief_omits: The sections-versus-explicit-binders mechanism, the section name, the exact variable sets per section, the binder-order change, the measured timings, the cross-reference to PR #42214, and the 'Generated with Claude Code' note.
